title: Record decision: Amex statements are PDF-only; retire M2 Amex CSV, promote M7 Amex PDF to P0
description:
DECISION (user, 2026-10-01): Amex statements will be downloaded as PDF from the mobile app. The app offers PDF export only; the web app's CSV/OFX/QBO options are not part of the workflow. Settles the Amex half of the acquisition policy in LifeOS-s9t.

WHY, and why not web automation: Amex NL has no public API (ARCH:101, CONFIRMED). Automating the web export would require driving the web UI with a persistent Playwright profile - 2FA re-prompts, session timeouts, DOM churn, stored bank credentials, and standard anti-scraping terms - for a few PDFs a month. iOS Shortcuts cannot reach another app's sandbox, so the app-PDF cannot be auto-saved either. There is no gap to close, because the app PDF already reconciles to delta 0 against the statement's own printed totals.

CONSEQUENCES, all recorded in docs/research/02-amex-nl.md and docs/research/11-real-export-verification.md:
- M2 (Amex CSV, LifeOS-7) is retired: there is no CSV source.
- M7 (Amex PDF, LifeOS-12) is the only Amex path and is raised to P0.
- ARCH:779's PDF->CSV fingerprint test is moot, and so is the open question of whether a CSV's single date equals the PDF's transaction or processing date. No CSV exists to reconcile.
- ARCH:122 ('PDF is the better source, not the fallback') is understated: for Amex, PDF is the ONLY source.
- ARCH:127's retention rationale strengthens - archived PDFs are the only durable copy.
- The measured fact that transaction and processing dates differ on 35% of Amex rows still matters: it is why raw_posting_date is load-bearing in the PDF path (LifeOS-hwv).

STILL OPEN, deliberately: Revolut and Rabobank are NOT settled by this decision. Rabobank is planned via Enable Banking PSD2 (LifeOS-10). Revolut depends on the production probe in LifeOS-17, after which the Revolut PDF may be needed only for pre-consent history.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in docs/research/02-amex-nl.md and docs/11, with M2 retired and M7 promoted. No Amex CSV adapter is built. ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md states that PDF is Amex's only source, not a fallback.

title: Decide statement acquisition policy: app-PDF only, or webapp CSV, or automation
description:
User reports the Amex, Revolut and Rabobank MOBILE apps offer PDF export only; the web apps offer additional formats (CSV, and OFX/QBO for Amex) but the user will not rely on the web app for routine use. This single choice determines the whole ingestion roadmap.

Consequences already identified:
- If app-PDF only: M7 (Amex PDF) becomes the primary AND only Amex path and must be raised from p2 to p0. M2 (Amex CSV, LifeOS-7) has little value and should be re-scoped or retired. The cross-format PDF->CSV fingerprint test at ARCH:779 becomes moot, and so does the Amex single-date question raised in docs/research/11 section 3.1.
- The ARCH:127 rationale that archived exports are the only durable copy becomes STRONGER, since PDF is the only source and Rabobank coverage from these exports starts 2026-06-01.
- Revolut CSV cannot be assumed to carry a stable id (R07:15, EB-SETUP:152) if CSV is only an occasional manual path.

Open sub-question assigned to research: whether the web apps' export can be triggered programmatically (discoverable XHR endpoint vs form POST vs headless-browser required), and whether any European open-banking aggregator reaches Revolut NL. See docs/research/11 section 7 for what stays untested either way.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md with the reasoning, the affected milestones re-prioritised, and the follow-up beads updated or closed.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Research summary feeding this decision. Bottom line: do NOT automate the web app. Ranked, with what is actually established versus merely asserted:

1. RABOBANK - already solved, web app irrelevant. Enable Banking PSD2 gives transactions programmatically; this repo already committed to it. ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md additionally establishes that personal Rabo accounts get CSV/PDF only, and that CAMT.053 is a business-channel product (RDC / SWIFT FileAct / RIB Pro / RBB) requiring a commercial agreement. So: no personal CAMT, and PSD2 gives transactions rather than statement files.

2. REVOLUT - the real open question. Revolut states there is no public API for personal accounts; the Business API is commercial and the Open Banking API is for licensed TPPs. So the realistic path is PSD2 via an aggregator. See LifeOS-17 for the Enable Banking lead and its verification status. Fallback aggregators (Plaid, TrueLayer) were suggested by research but are UNVERIFIED for NL and may be aimed at businesses rather than consumers; do not plan on them.

3. AMEX - no API, and the repo has already recorded this as CONFIRMED (ARCH:101). Automating the web export would mean driving the web UI with a persistent Playwright profile. High maintenance, breaks on 2FA re-prompts, session timeouts and DOM churn, needs stored credentials, and the standard anti-scraping terms apply. Not worth it for a few statements a month, and there is no gap to close: the app PDF already reconciles to delta 0.

4. MOBILE AUTOMATION - not viable. iOS Shortcuts cannot touch another app's sandbox or UI, so there is no way to auto-save the PDF the app produces; Android Tasker could drive the UI but breaks on app UI changes and 2FA.

LEGAL: PSD2 is a statutory right (Art. 66) exercised via consent-based OAuth, so an aggregator is materially safer than web scraping, which typically breaches ToS and requires storing bank credentials.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DECISION: if Revolut is reachable via PSD2, the Revolut PDF is only needed for pre-consent history and the 'no stable transaction ID' problem at D-REVOLET-ID largely disappears. That would make M7 (Amex PDF) the only PDF importer that matters and would justify raising it from p2 to p0. Confirm via LifeOS-17 before re-prioritising.

comments.text:
PARTIALLY SETTLED. The Amex half is decided: PDF-only from the mobile app, recorded as LifeOS-18. Do not close this bead yet - Revolut is still open pending the production probe in LifeOS-17, and Rabobank's path (Enable Banking PSD2) is planned but unbuilt.

If yes, Revolut PDF is needed only for pre-consent history and M8 (LifeOS-13) becomes a PSD2 adapter rather than a file importer. If no, Revolut is PDF-only with no stable transaction IDs, which is the same position as Amex, and D-REVOLET-ID's assumption that Revolut's CSV has a stable 'id' column is dead.

title: SAFETY INCIDENT: destroyed live Enable Banking private key
description:
SAFETY INCIDENT (2026-09-30): destroyed a live Enable Banking private key.

WHAT HAPPENED
  An agent ran `rm -rf .eb-keys/` assuming the directory held only its own
  test artifacts. It actually held a live RSA private key and self-signed
  certificate. The certificate had ALREADY been uploaded to the Enable
  Banking Control Panel for app 6afaac81-877b-40d8-a2ad-554b450f23e0.

CONSEQUENCES
  - Private key permanently lost. A private key cannot be regenerated.
    No git history (gitignored), no backup, no trash.
  - The app was orphaned: a PSD2 app has authority only via the key that
    signs its JWTs.
  - The user had recorded the app_id only in the deleted file, so could not
    locate the app in the Control Panel.
  - MITIGATING: the app was inert. No consent flow was ever completed, no
    bank account connected, and with the key destroyed nobody could use it.
    No data exposure. It was avoidable lost time, not a security incident.

ROOT CAUSES
  1. Deleted files whose provenance was never verified. The .gitignore entry
     was used to justify it - a category error. Gitignore means UNTRACKED,
     not MINE. It is also exactly why there was no recovery path.
  2. keygen defaulted to writing credentials INSIDE the working tree, which
     made live secrets look like disposable build output.
  3. rm -rf was run with no manifest, so nothing showed what it would destroy.
  4. The app_id was not recorded anywhere except the file that was deleted.

FIXES SHIPPED
  - keygen now writes to ~/.config/lifeos/eb/ and REFUSES to write inside the repo.
  - keygen writes a README.txt next to the key explaining it is unrecoverable.
  - keygen prints the exact command to record the app_id, as step 2 of 4.
  - tools/rm_guard.py: dry run by default, manifest before deleting, blocks
    protected paths, blocks out-of-tree targets, blocks credential deletion
    without an explicit --i-created-this-session acknowledgement.
  - SAFETY.md: incident write-up, six hard rules, and a recovery runbook.
  - AGENTS.md: safety rules at the very top, above the generated beads block,
    so a future agent reads them before touching anything.

RULES FOR FUTURE AGENTS
  1. Never rm -rf in this working tree. Use tools/rm_guard.py.
  2. Never delete a file you did not create this session without reading it.
  3. Never write credentials inside this repository.
  4. No bulk glob deletes in the working tree.
  5. State what you are about to delete, and why, before doing it.
  6. Record external identifiers the moment they are issued, in two places,
     one of them outside the repo.

VERIFICATION
  - rm_guard tested: dry run, --force, protected path, out-of-tree target,
    credential blocking.
  - keygen tested: refuses repo paths, correct perms, README written,
    verify passes on the generated pair.
design: Everything in this bead exists because an agent ran a bare rm -rf on files it had not created. A private key cannot be regenerated, so the loss was permanent. The fixes are structural, not advisory: the tooling now refuses the unsafe operations rather than trusting the agent to remember not to do them.
acceptance_criteria: SAFETY.md exists with incident + 6 hard rules + recovery runbook. tools/rm_guard.py tested (dry run, force, protected path, out-of-tree, credential block). probe_aspsps.py keygen writes to ~/.config/lifeos/eb/ and refuses repo paths. AGENTS.md carries the rules above the generated block. Fresh keypair generated and verified.
close_reason: Remediation verified complete: SAFETY.md, tools/rm_guard.py, out-of-repo keygen, AGENTS.md warning, and recurrence fix a178af5 all present and checked.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
REMEDIATION VERIFIED COMPLETE - closing. Every acceptance item checked against the working tree, not assumed:
- SAFETY.md exists, documenting the incident, hard rules and recovery runbook.
- tools/rm_guard.py exists and carries protected-path patterns and credential handling.
- tools/probe_aspsps.py writes keys to ~/.config/lifeos/eb/ and no longer defaults to a repo-local .eb-keys/ - the exact cause of this incident. Comment at line 57 records the change, and LEGACY_REPO_KEY_DIR at line 78 exists only as a migration search path.

title: M7: Amex PDF importer (7-year history)
description:
PDF is the BETTER Amex source, not the emergency fallback: 7 years of history vs ~6
months for CSV, itemized per transaction, and it carries BOTH transaction date and process date plus
FX detail. CSV has one date and a short window. The original brief listed AmexPDFImporter last; it
should be treated as first-class.

  - pdfplumber-based extraction
  - Separate parsing step from field mapping (the Firefly III AbstractTransaction lesson)
  - Tier 3 confidence weighted DOWN for PDF (extraction is noisier: column alignment, OCR)
  - Critical property: importing a 7-year PDF and then a 6-month CSV must be NON-DESTRUCTIVE -
    the CSV rows already exist from the PDF and fingerprint-match

  CONTINGENT on LifeOS-2: if the PDF text layer is scanned images rather than selectable text, this
  becomes an OCR project and must be rescoped before starting.
design: The PDF/CSV overlap test is the single most important test in this milestone - it is the proof that archiving exports is a safe strategy rather than a source of duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: A 7-year PDF imports. Then a 6-month CSV of the same data creates ZERO new entries and every CSV row is accounted for as a fingerprint match. Original foreign amount + exchange rate are captured when present.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
GATE CLEARED: the Amex PDF text layer is selectable, not scanned. M7 was contingent on this (ARCH:861-862, RECO:148 risk 3) and the answer is a clean GO - all four statements extract as ordered structured text, no OCR, and the 7-year PDF path is now the primary Amex source.

Priority question raised in LifeOS-s9t: if the Amex app is the routine download path and it offers PDF only, this milestone is the ONLY Amex path and should be raised from p2 to p0, with M2 (LifeOS-7, Amex CSV) re-scoped or retired.

Findings that bear directly on this importer's design are in docs/research/11-real-export-verification.md sections 3.1-3.3: transaction vs processing date diverge on 35% of rows; credits are marked by a separate 'CR' line and are NOT sign-distinguished, so the card payment must be separated from refunds by description; and the balance identity runs Vorig + Debiteringen - Crediteringen = Nieuw, opposite to a current account.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
DEDUP AND PARSING OBLIGATIONS for this milestone, measured against the four real statements. Full evidence: docs/research/11-real-export-verification.md. A working reference parser is in tools/bankparse/amex.py (research tooling, stdlib only; its self-test is the template for the acceptance test below).

1. TIER-3 FINGERPRINT IS MANDATORY, NOT FALLBACK. The Amex PDF carries no stable transaction ID, confirmed empirically rather than inferred. ARCH:17-18 and R02:139 are right about this.

2. occurrence_index IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A SAFETY NET. The 2026-06-23 statement contains SNCB-NMBS SNCB-NMBS BRUXELLES for -13,40 on 2026-06-12 TWICE. That is the 'two genuinely identical transactions, same day, same merchant' case ARCH:582-584 calls impossible to dedupe automatically. It is real, and it is the only such pair in 121 rows - but one is enough to require occurrence_index.

3. THE NORMALISATION MARGIN IS THIN, AND THIS IS THE REAL RISK. The same statement also contains NMBS NMBS BRUXELLES 12,80 and SNCB-NMBS SNCB-NMBS BRUXELLES 13,40. A description normalisation aggressive enough to merge the identical pair would also collapse these two distinct train purchases into one. ARCH:558's rule (strip a trailing '* # REF:...') is nowhere near aggressive enough to reach this, so current behaviour is safe - but the margin is narrow and any future normalisation change must be tested against these two rows specifically. Fingerprint over-normalisation silently DELETES real spend, which is worse than a duplicate.

4. raw_posting_date IS LOAD-BEARING. Transaction and processing dates differ on 42 of 121 rows (35%). R07:41 wrongly says they are equal; see LifeOS-hwv. Consequence for dedup: ARCH:559 keys the fingerprint on raw_date alone, so the choice of which date becomes raw_date is now a frozen decision - get it right before shipping, because the fingerprint is frozen by hash (ARCH:590) and changing it later orphans every stored fingerprint.

5. THE SIGN FLIP MUST BE CONSISTENT ACROSS RE-PARSES. Source is charges-positive; the ledger is debits-negative. A re-parse that classifies a row differently changes its signed amount and therefore its fingerprint, producing a duplicate rather than a match. See LifeOS-lcy.

6. A MISSED 'CR' LINE SILENTLY INFLATES SPENDING. Credits carry no sign in the source: the amount is positive for both charges and credits, and a credit is marked by a line containing only 'CR' BENEATH the amount. Each statement mixes the monthly card payment (HARTELIJK BEDANKT VOOR UW BETALING: 721,35 / 765,67 / 332,43 / 272,48) with 0-3 genuine refunds. Book a card payment as a purchase and spending is overstated by the full payment, with nothing to flag it.

7. USE THE STATEMENT'S OWN TOTALS AS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. This is what caught every parsing bug during verification, and it is cheap: extracted charges == printed Debiteringen; extracted credits == printed Crediteringen; Vorig saldo + Debiteringen - Crediteringen == Nieuw saldo; Nieuw saldo == Te betalen. All four held at delta 0 on all four statements. Note the identity runs the OPPOSITE way to a current account - a charge increases the amount owed - so a generic balance check will not work (see LifeOS-2rg).

8. RE-IMPORT SAFETY MUST BE TESTED EXPLICITLY, and the PDF path is the awkward one. D-OCCURRENCE-PDF-TIEBREAK (R07:64-65) uses hash(raw_line) % 10000 because a PDF has no reliable line number. Importing the same PDF twice must yield 0 new journal_entry rows; that is the test ARCH:777 states for CSV and it has never been run against a PDF.

9. TWO THINGS NOT TO DESIGN AROUND. Amex never emits pending transactions, so status must never be 'pending' (ARCH:506, R07:38). And the foreign-currency column is EMPTY in all four statements with no non-EUR code anywhere, so foreign_amount stays null from this source - do not build the acceptance criteria around FX without a real foreign purchase.

Reference: the parser reduced 4 statements to 121 rows with every total at delta 0, and re-running is byte-identical.

title: M1: double-entry schema + manual transactions
description:
Schema from docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md section E, with the review corrections applied:
  - DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED balance trigger. NOT a row-level FOR EACH ROW trigger, which
    would reject every valid transaction because it checks the sum before the second line exists.
  - no 'direction' column - the sign is the direction, and a direction column contradicts a signed
    amount in two different columns.
  - no user_id - single user, and it is noise on every row and every query.
  - no account.provider_account_id - duplicated by provider_account_link, and its unique constraint
    would break when one card is visible to two providers (exactly the Amex + Google Wallet case).
  - no journal_entry.source_record_id - circular FK with source_record.journal_entry_id.
  - no empty security/holding/cost_basis_lot tables. The seam is account_type='investment' plus
    nullable security_id/units/price_per_unit on journal_line, using the same unconstrained-BIGINT
    pattern as the future attachment_id/goal_id.
  - pg_trgm extension enabled.

Then: manual transaction CRUD through the API + the simplest possible UI.
design: Proving the double-entry balance invariant before any ingestion complexity sits on top of it is the entire point of this milestone.
acceptance_criteria: A two-line entry commits successfully. An unbalanced entry is REJECTED AT COMMIT (not per-row). No user table. Manual expense CRUD works end to end. Every balance invariant test passes.

title: M0: repo skeleton, Docker Compose, invariants, CI
description:
First implementation block. Nothing stores real data yet.

Deliverables per docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md section D:
  - backend/ (core/, finance/ with domain, ingestion, api, background)
  - frontend/ (React + TS + Vite + Tailwind + shadcn/ui)
  - docker-compose.yml: db, api, worker
  - Makefile, pyproject.toml (uv), lint config
  - AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md (<=200 lines), invariants.yaml
  - CI: ruff, mypy --strict, pytest, importlinter, invariant check, zero-egress test

The four non-negotiable invariants, machine-checked:
  1. raw_data_immutable - source_record.raw_data and raw_description are never updated or deleted
  2. no_cross_schema_fk  - no foreign keys across Postgres schemas
  3. migrations_immutable - applied migrations are never edited
  4. fingerprint_frozen  - finance/ingestion/fingerprint.py is hash-pinned

The zero-egress test is the distinctive one: run the app with --network=none and strace -e network,
assert zero connect() calls, while file import still works. Proves no telemetry AND offline operation.
design: Guardrails BEFORE data. An AI-vibe-coded project breaks invariants silently without these. This is the highest-leverage non-feature work in the whole roadmap.
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up brings up a healthy db/api/worker. CI green on a fresh clone. A deliberate attempt to violate each invariant FAILS CI - a negative test per invariant, not just a positive check.
close_reason: M0 complete. Acceptance criteria met: (1) 'docker compose up' brings up healthy db/api/worker/frontend under -p lifeos; (2) make ci exits 0 on the committed tree; (3) each of the four invariants has a negative test that FAILS when deliberately violated - 30 such tests, plus a self-testing dependency gate. Executed as four phases after the first attempt was halted: LifeOS-by8 (backend), LifeOS-kv0 (frontend), LifeOS-pl7 (integration), plus the ARCHITECTURE.md and invariant-engine work already done. Two defects found but deliberately left unfixed, both filed: LifeOS-gsy (alembic.ini KeyError blocks 'upgrade head', blocking for M1) and LifeOS-mkj (psycopg wheel variant).

title: Decide deployment topology (VPS / home server / hosted Postgres)
description:
GATING. Blocks M0.

The app needs a host that is always on, plus secure access from laptop and phone.
Hosting locally on the laptop is not viable: when the laptop is off, the app is unreachable.

Requirements:
  - always available (laptop may be off)
  - Docker Compose: db + api + worker
  - a LONG-RUNNING worker process (Enable Banking has no webhooks, so sync is polled every few hours)
  - PostgreSQL with pg_trgm and DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint triggers
  - automated backups with point-in-time recovery (losing a financial ledger is unacceptable)
  - minimal lock-in, minimal third parties, EU data residency, low cost

Evaluate: small EU VPS (Hetzner/Netcup/etc), home server/NAS, Supabase or other managed Postgres,
PaaS container + managed DB. See docs/research/10-hosting.md for the full comparison.

Specific question to answer: is Supabase viable given it cannot run an arbitrary long-running
worker container?
design: Tailscale is the likely answer for remote access: no public exposure, no reverse proxy to maintain, works for laptop and phone. Confirm the free tier covers the device count.
acceptance_criteria: Topology chosen and written up in docs/adr/0001-deployment-topology.md. Docker Compose service list fixed. Backup + monthly restore-test procedure documented. Secrets approach fixed (OS keyring vs platform env vars).
close_reason: Deployment topology decided: Netcup VPS 500 G12 Amsterdam (€5.91/mo) with Docker Compose (db+api+worker+tailscale), restic+age backups, Tailscale for access. Supabase rejected: no free-tier backups, PITR costs 40/mo, cannot run long-running worker. ADR written to docs/adr/0001-deployment-topology.md with data transfer procedure from MacBook to VPS.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Evaluated deployment topology options per docs/research/10-hosting.md. Key finding: Supabase is NOT viable because free tier lacks automated backups, PITR is cost-prohibitive (~$140/mo), and it cannot run arbitrary long-running worker processes required for polling Enable Banking sync. Workaround (pg_cron + Edge Functions) hits CPU time limits and still requires an external host. Decided on Netcup VPS 500 G12 Amsterdam (€5.91/mo) with Docker Compose (db + api + worker + tailscale), restic + age encrypted backups with monthly restore verification, secrets in OS keyring, and Tailscale private mesh access. Development locally on Linux MacBook with simple pg_dump/pg_restore migration to VPS. Acceptance criteria fulfilled and documented in ADR 0001.

VERIFIED functionally: V1_PROVIDERS is exactly (enable_banking, amex_pdf, rabobank_pdf, revolut_pdf, manual); _FILE_ADAPTERS holds only amex_pdf; accepts_upload agrees with _FILE_ADAPTERS for every provider; amex_csv and revolut_csv appear nowhere on the live provider surface. amex_csv.py and revolut_csv.py remain on disk and exported, documented as retired but unreachable through the v1 provider list, because removing them is a separate undecided step.

NOTE on the egress test: it injects a local pure text extractor, since the real one is M7's pdfplumber seam and pdfplumber is not in the M0 dependency set. The test docstring now states plainly that it proves the offline path is telemetry-free and does NOT prove a real PDF was parsed, so ARCHITECTURE.md's no-telemetry claim is not over-extended.

title: S3: amex_pdf.py continuation lines replace the merchant description, corrupting hash-frozen fingerprints
description:
amex_pdf.py initialises description='' (:203-209) while keeping the real text in description_source. The continuation branch (:196) then does pending.description = f'{pending.description} {stripped}', and _finish (:293) PREFERS description — so the first continuation line REPLACES the merchant name instead of appending to it. Verified: in the S2 sample, 'HARTELIJK BEDANKT VOOR UW BETALING' vanished entirely and the description became 'CR'.

No existing test covers a continuation line (backend/finance/tests/integration/test_adapters.py:388-395 has none).

Why this matters more than it looks: the description feeds fingerprint.py, which is HASH-FROZEN and pinned in invariants.yaml. Over-normalised descriptions silently delete real spend from dedup — no error, wrong total.
design: Either append to description_source (the field that actually holds the full text) and have _finish prefer it, or drop the redundant description field. Prefer the former — the split field is the root cause. Add a continuation-line test at the same time; this defect and S2 share a fixture.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-line merchant description survives parsing intact, and a test asserts the full concatenated text reaches fingerprint input.
close_reason:
Fixed. A non-row line now appends to pending.description_source instead of replacing it, so a wrapped merchant description survives intact and the hash-frozen fingerprint sees the full text.

EVIDENCE: test_continuation_lines_append_to_description asserts both the merchant and its continuation are present. MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting the append to a replace fails test_adapters.py::TestAmexPdfRegression::test_continuation_lines_append_to_description. Note this axis is caught by the adapter regression test rather than the balance invariant, which is correct: the identity sums amounts, and description corruption does not change the sum.

title: S2: amex_pdf.py has no CR credit detection — card payment booked as a purchase
description:
amex_pdf.py has no equivalent of tools/bankparse/amex.py's CR_RE (line 40) / is_credit check (line 143), and _SECTION_HEADINGS (:76-93) does not list 'cr'. In Amex NL statements a credit is marked by a line containing only 'CR' printed BENEATH the amount — both purchases and refunds carry unsigned positive amounts, so the CR marker is the only way to tell them apart.

Verified consequence: a row in the format amex_pdf.py DOES accept, '2026-05-25  -72135  CR', books the monthly card payment as a DEBIT with the literal description 'CR'.

This is LifeOS-12 obligation #6 verbatim: 'A MISSED CR LINE SILENTLY INFLATES SPENDING — nothing to flag it.'

Note the two lanes agree on sign convention (both negative-is-debit, verified) — the divergence is credit DETECTION specifically, which is why this slipped through review.
design: Port CR_RE from tools/bankparse/amex.py:40 and its use at :143. lif-2 already documented the exact rule at amex.py:13-15 and emitted it in its parse reports ('A credit is identified by a line containing only CR beneath the amount').
acceptance_criteria: A test feeds a card-payment row with a following bare CR line and asserts a credit (positive/minor-unit direction), not a debit. Without the test this regresses silently.
close_reason:
Fixed. A bare 'CR' line beneath the amount is now detected (_CR_RE) and sets is_credit on the pending row; _finish then emits +amount for a credit and -amount for a debit under AmountSignConvention.SIGNED. This was the defect that booked the monthly card payment as a purchase.

EVIDENCE: test_bare_cr_line_marks_a_credit_positive asserts the card payment lands +72135 while a purchase lands -850; the balance-invariant fixture mixes the card payment with a genuine refund and asserts BOTH are credits, since doc 11 §3.2 shows the two are separable by description only. MUTATION-VERIFIED: changing _CR_RE to a never-matching pattern fails 9 of the 12 balance-invariant tests, including the mixed-credit split and the card-payment gap of -144270.

title: S1: amex_pdf.py row regex cannot match a real Amex NL statement
description:
backend/finance/ingestion/adapters/amex_pdf.py _ROW_START (lines 49-52) requires (?P<year>\d{4}) and a single leading date. Real Dutch Amex NL pdftotext -layout rows are '24.05.26  25.05.26  <desc>  <amount>' — a 2-digit year and TWO dates (Transactiedatum / Datum verwerkt). Verified by the consolidation review: all real-format sample rows fail to match, so every row falls through to the description-continuation branch and the parser returns 0 records with an empty failure list. No error is raised.

This is the ONLY Amex path per LifeOS-18 (closed, P0).

Note extract_pdf_text (:96-110) is an explicit documented placeholder ('a real implementation needs pdfplumber, which M7 introduces'), so the mismatch has not bitten yet. But the row regex must be fixed before pdfplumber is wired in, or the P0 path will silently import nothing.

A verified working reference exists in the same repo: tools/bankparse/amex.py:39 ROW_RE = r'^\s*(\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2})\s+(\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2})\s+(.*)$' — two 2-digit dates, validated against four real statements by the lif-2 lane.
design:
Port the two-date row regex and date handling from tools/bankparse/amex.py rather than inventing a third format. Decide which of Transactiedatum / Datum verwerkt is the posting date — that choice determines the raw_date vs raw_posting_date field the dedup layer depends on (see LifeOS-3pe / docs/research/07-dedup-contingencies.md:41, which is stale and contradicted by docs/research/11).

Two options: (a) port lif-2's verified logic into amex_pdf.py, or (b) explicitly mark amex_pdf non-functional until M7 so it cannot be mistaken for working. Option (a) is preferred — a working parser already exists.
acceptance_criteria: Given a realistic pdftotext -layout Amex NL fixture, amex_pdf.py returns a non-zero record count and a non-empty failure list on garbage input. A regression test asserts records > 0 for the real format, so this cannot silently regress again.
close_reason:
Fixed. _ROW_START in amex_pdf.py now matches the verified Dutch Amex NL pdftotext -layout row: two DD.MM.YY dates (Transactiedatum, Datum verwerkt), then description, then unsigned European amount. The previous regex required a 4-digit year with a spelled or numeric month and matched zero rows of a real statement.

EVIDENCE: a real-format fixture must parse non-zero (test_adapters.py::TestAmexPdfRegression::test_nonzero_parse_for_real_dutch_layout); 2-digit years expand row-locally via a century pivot, not a global default. MUTATION-VERIFIED: disabling the amount matcher fails 13 tests across the egress, dedup and balance-invariant suites, so the row wiring is load-bearing rather than incidentally green.

title: Fix alembic.ini: missing logging sections break 'alembic upgrade head'
description:
FOUND DURING P3 (bead LifeOS-pl7). NOT fixed - the integration lane correctly stayed out of files it does not own.

backend/core/alembic.ini and backend/finance/alembic.ini are both missing the [loggers], [handlers] and [formatters] sections that alembic's fileConfig() indexes by literal name. 'alembic upgrade head' therefore dies with:

    KeyError: 'formatters'

BEFORE it even opens a database connection. This makes M1 (bead LifeOS-6, the double-entry schema) unrunnable the moment anyone tries to apply a real migration.

The Makefile currently works around it by prepending the missing sections to a temp copy under /tmp. The committed files are untouched by that workaround. Fix at the source: add the missing sections to both .ini files and drop the Makefile workaround.

IMPACT: blocking for M1. Not blocking for M0 - nothing stores real data yet and both alembic versions/ dirs still hold only .gitkeep.

VERIFY after fixing:
  cd backend/core && uv run alembic upgrade head     (expect no KeyError)
  cd backend/finance && uv run alembic upgrade head
  make migrate                                       (expect the temp-copy workaround gone)
close_reason:
Fixed at the source. Both backend/core/alembic.ini and backend/finance/alembic.ini now declare the [loggers], [handlers] and [formatters] registries that logging.config.fileConfig() indexes by literal name. The Makefile 'migrate' and 'migrate-status' recipes no longer prepend those sections to a temp copy; the temp copy now carries only the substituted database URL (still required: env.py reads sqlalchemy.url from the ini and never consults LIFEOS_DATABASE_URL), and the stale WORKAROUND NOTE is replaced by an accurate one.

VERIFIED: (a) configparser confirms all three registries present with non-empty keys in both files; (b) logging.config.fileConfig() - the exact call that raised KeyError: 'formatters' - now succeeds against both committed inis; (c) 'alembic -c core/alembic.ini upgrade head --sql' and the finance equivalent both complete cleanly (BEGIN; COMMIT;), proving env.py, the config load and the revision-tree walk all work against the committed files.

NOT VERIFIED: the DB-connected 'alembic upgrade head'. Nothing listens on localhost:5432 in this environment and both alembic/versions/ dirs still contain only .gitkeep, so there is no migration to apply anyway. Unblocks LifeOS-6 (M1), whose blocker was that 'alembic upgrade head' died with KeyError before opening a connection.

title: Apply real-export findings (doc 11) to the design docs
description:
Merge of six doc-correction beads raised by the real-export verification (docs/research/11-real-export-verification.md). All six are one pass over the design docs and were split only because the findings arrived separately.

1. CORRECT R07:41. It claims Amex 'raw_posting_date vs raw_date | same (posted only) | Nullable, no issue'. Measured: the two columns differ on 42 of 121 rows (35%) - 10/32, 10/33, 11/28, 11/28. raw_posting_date is load-bearing for Amex.

2. DOCUMENT THE AMEX SIGN FLIP. ARCH:366 sets the ledger as debits-negative; 02-amex-nl.md:59 sets the Amex source as charges-positive. The inversion is written down nowhere. Worse, in the PDF the amount column carries no sign at all - a credit is marked by a lone 'CR' line beneath the amount, and each statement mixes the card payment (721,35 / 765,67 / 332,43 / 272,48) with 0-3 real refunds. Payment vs refund is separable by DESCRIPTION only.

3. PROVIDER ENUM (decision). ARCH:288-289 has no revolut_pdf and no rabobank_pdf, so the schema cannot represent the only files the user has. Revolut PDF appears nowhere in any doc. Decide: add the enum values, or record via ADR that these files are research-only.

4. BALANCE INVARIANT (decision). A current account satisfies prev + credits - debits = closing; Amex satisfies Vorig + Debiteringen - Crediteringen = Nieuw, the opposite direction. No column stores a statement balance, so this is asserted nowhere. It is what caught every parsing bug during verification, so define it per account type and make it a required adapter acceptance test.

5. RABOBANK TYPE CODES. No enum exists. 24-code legend printed on the last page of every statement; 11 codes observed (ba bg bv cb db ei ga id sb tb we), all legend-defined, 'we' truncated in the source. Unknown codes must warn, not guess.

6. REVOLUT DEPOSIT-TO-IBAN (decision). One file covers two products and two own IBANs (NL69REVO...1997, LT5032500...9880) and never states which IBAN the Deposit belongs to. tools/bankparse/revolut.py currently infers it and flags it as inferred. Decide: separate account, distinct source_record status, or user-confirmed inference. Note import_batch has a single account_id (ARCH:287) but this file needs two.

Also record: the printed 'Periode' is advisory, not a filter - real statements carry transactions dated the day before the period opens, so filtering on period bounds would drop genuine spend. And the Amex provider enum already had amex_pdf, so item 3 is about Revolut and Rabobank only.
acceptance_criteria: ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md and 02/07/09 reflect all six corrections with citations to docs/research/11. Items 3, 4 and 6 are recorded as explicit decisions, not silent guesses. The balance invariant appears in invariants.yaml and is a required adapter acceptance test.
close_reason:
All six items applied, each as an explicit decision rather than a silent correction.

1. R07:41 CORRECTED. docs/research/07:46 no longer claims 'Amex: same (posted only) | Nullable, no issue'. Replaced with the measured fact: the two columns differ on 42 of 121 rows (35%) -- 10/32, 10/33, 11/28, 11/28 -- so raw_posting_date is load-bearing for Amex, with the worked 16.06.26/17.06.26 example.
2. SIGN FLIP RECORDED as ADR 0003 Decision 1, plus a new section 3a in docs/research/02-amex-nl.md with a three-row convention table. Records that the PDF carries NO sign at all -- direction is a lone CR marker line beneath the amount -- and the second inversion hiding behind it: CR separates credits from charges, NOT card payments from refunds.
3. PROVIDER ENUM DECIDED in ADR 0002: enable_banking, amex_pdf, rabobank_pdf, revolut_pdf, manual. amex_csv RETIRED, revolut_csv DEFERRED (its stable id is unverified), google_wallet EXCLUDED. rabobank_pdf and revolut_pdf are user-confirmed v1 paths with no FileAdapter yet -- listed, not uploadable. Four rejected alternatives recorded.
4. BALANCE IDENTITY RECORDED as ADR 0003 Decision 2, per account type, and is now a REQUIRED ADAPTER ACCEPTANCE TEST (backend/finance/tests/integration/test_balance_invariant.py, 12 tests). The checker in scripts/check_invariants.py supports only forbid_regex/hash/manifest, none of which execute a parse or compare a number, and the right-hand side lives in the uploaded file rather than the repo -- so an entry expressed with them would be decorative and an entry no checker evaluates always passes. The reasoning is recorded in ADR 0003 and as a comment-only block in invariants.yaml. No new invariant kind was invented to satisfy the acceptance criterion.
5. RABOBANK TYPE CODES RECORDED as ADR 0003 Decision 3: full 24-entry legend transcribed, all 11 observed codes (ba bg bv cb db ei ga id sb tb we), the 'we' truncation noted verbatim, and the rule that an unknown code warns and never guesses. Recorded as a definition for M1 (LifeOS-6), not live code, because M1's schema does not exist yet.
6. REVOLUT DEPOSIT-TO-IBAN RECORDED as ADR 0003 Decision 4 with the user's decision: Current and Deposit are separate accounts, ambiguous ownership is HELD and never inferred. Consequences for import_batch.account_id spelled out, including that held rows are never written under a guessed id because that would require rewriting under raw_data_immutable.

ALSO RECORDED: the printed Periode is advisory and never an import predicate (doc 11 section 5.3).

VERIFIED: doc 11 itself untouched (empty diff); 4/4 invariants pass; 455 tests pass; every docs/adr/ reference in backend/, frontend/ and the design docs now resolves to a file that exists (0002 was cited by two source files but did not exist before this work). Every surviving amex_csv/revolut_csv/google_wallet mention in the docs is a deliberate retirement/deferral/exclusion note.

title: Document and test the Amex source-to-ledger sign flip
description:
Two conventions collide and the flip between them is written down nowhere. docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md:366 fixes the ledger convention as 'Debits negative, credits positive'. docs/research/02-amex-nl.md:59 fixes the Amex source convention as 'charges positive, payments/credits negative'. The adapters must invert Amex amounts to reach the ledger convention, but no doc states this.

Worse, in the Amex PDF the amount column carries no sign at all: charges and credits are both positive, and a credit is marked by a line containing only 'CR' beneath the amount. The credit section mixes the monthly card payment with genuine refunds, so payment and refund must be separated by DESCRIPTION, not sign. Per-statement counts are in docs/research/11 section 3.2: payments 721,35 / 765,67 / 332,43 / 272,48, plus 1 to 3 refunds each.

Note the card payment was identified by the literal string 'HARTELIJK BEDANKT VOOR UW BETALING', which held for all four statements, but that is a second brittle string to learn alongside the Rabobank 'American Express' rule at ARCH:626.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit, tested adapter rule documents the inversion and the CR-marker detection. The card-payment vs refund distinction is a tested rule, not a comment.

title: Add revolut_pdf and rabobank_pdf to the provider enum, or record PDF-only as the path
description:
The provider CHECK constraint at docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md:288-289 is: enable_banking | amex_csv | amex_pdf | revolut_csv | manual | google_wallet. There is no revolut_pdf and no rabobank_pdf. The SourceAdapter comment at ARCH:146 and the adapter list at ARCH:187 match the same gap.

Revolut PDF is mentioned nowhere in any doc: no adapter, no enum value, no assumption, no open question. Yet it is the only Revolut format supplied, and the only full-year source (2026-01-01 to 10-01) against Rabobank's 2026-06 start. ARCH:101 treats the 7-year PDF path as Amex-only and ARCH:118 assumes Revolut arrives as CSV with a stable id.

Separately, no Rabobank file-import path exists at all: Rabobank is planned as Enable Banking API only (ARCH:99, LifeOS-10), with no PDF or CSV adapter and no enum value.

The schema currently cannot represent the only data the user actually has.
acceptance_criteria: Either revolut_pdf and rabobank_pdf are added to the CHECK constraint, the SourceAdapter comment, and the adapter layout, or an explicit ADR records that these files are research-only and not import paths, with the reasoning. The Revolut 2-products-in-1-file problem (docs/research/11 section 3.6) is addressed in the same change.

title: Correct R07:41: Amex transaction date and processing date are NOT equal
description:
docs/research/07-dedup-contingencies.md:41 states for Amex: 'raw_posting_date vs raw_date | same (posted only) | Nullable, no issue'. Measured against the four real statements in docs/research/11 section 3.1, the two Amex date columns differ on 42 of 121 rows (35%): 10/32, 10/33, 11/28, 11/28. Example: transaction date 16.06.26, processed 17.06.26; 10.06.26 processed 12.06.26.

raw_posting_date is load-bearing for Amex, not cosmetic. R07:41 is factually wrong and any adapter or test written from it will silently mis-handle a third of Amex rows.
acceptance_criteria: R07:41 corrected to state the measured divergence, the row counts per statement cited, and a pointer to docs/research/11 section 3.1. Any test that assumed equality is updated or removed.

title: Activate Enable Banking production app; settle Revolut NL
description:
Create the Enable Banking PRODUCTION app and settle whether Revolut NL is supported.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM LifeOS-13
  LifeOS-13 (M8 Revolut) is the implementation. This bead is the go/no-go probe that
  gates it. Separating them means the implementation work is not blocked on a signup form.

BLOCKED ON: nothing. It is not on the critical path for the build. Rabobank is already
CONFIRMED and is sufficient for M1-M10. Do this when convenient, or when LifeOS-3
(deployment topology) has produced a real host to serve the legal pages from.

CURRENT STATE
  - Sandbox app 528ee4b1-cbbe-4116-b552-7e9dd6555fd2 is ACTIVE and probed. Rabobank
    CONFIRMED there. Credentials live in ~/.config/lifeos/eb/ (outside the repo).
  - No production app exists.
  - Enable Banking's production signup asks for 4 KYB fields: application description,
    data-protection email, privacy URL, terms URL. The ToS describes these as required
    only for the UNRESTRICTED (commercial) path, but only ONE form was offered and no
    restricted/unrestricted toggle was visible. Their docs may be out of date.

WORK ALREADY DONE (this bead just needs finishing)
  1. All four field values are prepared in docs/legal/ and in
     docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md under "Prepared answers".
  2. Privacy notice and terms written and committed (docs/legal/*.html). They describe
     actual behaviour: single user, self-hosted, no telemetry, no central data copy, PSD2
     consent revoked at the bank, backups are the operator's responsibility.
  3. Publish instructions written. Cheapest option is GitHub Pages from a small public repo.

STEPS
  1. In docs/legal/, replace YOUR-EMAIL-HERE in privacy.html and terms.html with an
     address that is actually monitored. It is the GDPR breach-notification contact.
  2. Publish the two pages so both URLs RESOLVE. The bar is "loads a real page", not
     "looks professional". Confirm both load.
  3. Create the production app in the Control Panel, pasting the prepared values.
  4. Record the new production app_id IMMEDIATELY, in two places, one outside the repo
     (SAFETY.md Rule 6). Write it to ~/.config/lifeos/eb/app_id.prod and note it in
     docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md.
  5. Run:  python3 tools/probe_aspsps.py --app-id <prod-uuid> probe
  6. Compare the production NL list against the sandbox list.
  7. Update docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md and close this bead.

IMPORTANT - REUSE THE EXISTING KEYPAIR
  Do NOT run `keygen` again. The sandbox and production apps can share the single keypair
  in ~/.config/lifeos/eb/. Generating a second one is how the earlier incident happened:
  multiple keypairs means it is ambiguous which private key matches the uploaded
  certificate, and a mismatch is invisible until the API returns 401.

ALSO WORTH ASKING ENABLE BANKING
  "Is restricted mode (personal use, own accounts only) still available as a separate
  signup path, and do the privacy/terms URLs apply to it?" The ToS permits it free. A
  one-line answer saves guessing.

ACCEPTANCE
  - docs/legal/*.html have a real contact email and both URLs resolve.
  - Production app exists and is Active.
  - Production app_id recorded in ~/.config/lifeos/eb/app_id.prod and in
    docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md.
  - Production ASPSP list captured to docs/research/ as evidence.
  - Revolut question is either ANSWERED, or recorded as unanswerable via Enable Banking
    with the GoCardless Bank Account Data fallback adopted.
  - docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md updated; this bead closed.

OUTCOME DOES NOT CHANGE THE SCHEMA
  Revolut present -> API adapter. Revolut absent -> CSV importer (Revolut's CSV has a
  stable `id` column, so Tier-1 dedup applies). Either way the ledger is unchanged: it is
  provider-agnostic by design and only the IdentityResolver is provider-aware.
design: Deliberately split from LifeOS-13 (the implementation) so building Revolut is not blocked on a signup form. Rabobank is CONFIRMED and sufficient for M1-M10, so this is not on the critical path. REUSE the existing keypair - never run keygen again.
acceptance_criteria: Legal pages published and resolving; production app Active; prod app_id recorded in ~/.config/lifeos/eb/app_id.prod AND docs/ENABLE-BANKING-SETUP.md; production ASPSP list captured as evidence; Revolut either answered or fallback adopted; docs updated and bead closed.

title: M6: replay-from-raw
description:
Turn raw retention into an actual safety net, not a promise.

  - CLI: replay --batch-id=N re-runs the entire pipeline from import_batch.raw_payload
  - import_batch records raw bytes + sha256 + parser version
  - Enables: schema changes that affect normalization, categorization rule changes, and full rebuild
    after any bug in the pipeline

  This is the mitigation for risk #9 (schema churn during vibe-coding destroying real financial
  history) and the answer to the Amex 6-month CSV window, where archived exports are the only
  durable copy of anything.
design: Requires import_batch.raw_payload to never be deleted. That is a P0 invariant from M0, and this milestone is what proves it has teeth.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting every journal_entry and journal_line, then running replay, reproduces the ledger exactly. Changing a category rule and replaying re-categorizes without re-importing the file. Done BEFORE any schema churn, as promised in the roadmap.

title: M4: transfer matching + the Amex card payment
description:
The correctness requirement. Once this works, spending totals are trustworthy.

  - transfer_match table (stored, never recomputed, with match_method + confidence + confirmed_at)
  - Own-account transfers: Rabobank <-> Revolut, excluded from spending
  - THE AMEX CASE: a EUR 50 Amex purchase is an expense on a liability account; a later Rabobank
    -50 'American Express' has NO matching row to link, because the liability balance simply falls.
    Synthesize the liability leg (is_synthesized, synthesized_reason='card_payment') so the entry
    balances and spending is 50 once, never 100.
  - SEPA direct debit vs own-account transfer: deterministic rule, else review queue
  - Nightly sweep for unmatched outbound legs whose other leg has not been imported yet
  - Review queue UX: CONFIRM / REJECT / IGNORE

  Deliberately NOT implemented: Hungarian one-to-one assignment (borrowed from BankingSync). It
  solves batched ambiguous matching, which does not exist at 3 accounts. Reconsider only if the
  review queue shows real ambiguous clusters.
design: Card-payment detection is ILIKE '%american express%' at confidence 0.95 with user rejection allowed, and it LEARNS: after confirmation the observed description is promoted to a rule. Brittle on day one, self-correcting by month three.
acceptance_criteria: THE HEADLINE TEST: Amex 50 purchase then Rabobank -50 -> total spending is 50, not 100. Both journal entries balance. Two EUR 50 transfers the same day produce 2 distinct transfer_match rows, not 1 merged pair. A SEPA DD to a third party is an expense with no transfer_match. An ambiguous DD-vs-transfer lands in the review queue rather than being guessed.

title: M2: Amex CSV import + fingerprint dedup
description:
The milestone that proves correctness, and the only ingestion path guaranteed to exist.

  - SourceAdapter protocol + AmexCsvAdapter (column mapping from the LifeOS-2 findings)
  - import_batch (retains raw_payload, never deleted) + source_record (immutable raw_data)
  - Normalization into journal_entry/journal_line, double-entry
  - Tier 3 fingerprint: SHA256 over canonicalised
    description|amount|currency|date|account_id|occurrence_index
  - occurrence_index via ROW_NUMBER() so two identical EUR 3.20 coffees produce TWO entries
  - The cross-batch UNIQUE index on (fingerprint, account_id)
  - Categorization deferred to M3 - everything lands uncategorized

Note: Amex has NO stable transaction IDs, so Tier 1 is unavailable here. This IS the Tier 3 path.
design: fingerprint.py is a pure function with no I/O so it is exhaustively unit-testable, and it is hash-frozen from the start. Changing it later invalidates every stored fingerprint - that is why it is an invariant.

title: normalize.py and fingerprint.py have DIVERGED trailing-marker patterns; comment claimed they shared one
description:
Found while closing LifeOS-dbn (its 'minor' item). The false comment is now corrected in normalize.py:44-56; this bead tracks the actual behaviour gap, which needs a decision.

THE FALSE CLAIM (now fixed):
normalize.py:45-47 asserted 'fingerprint.py does its own equivalent strip; both must agree, so the pattern lives in one place and fingerprint.py imports it.' Both halves were false. fingerprint.py imports only hashlib and re (fingerprint.py:31-34) - it does not import normalize. Verified.

THE REAL DIVERGENCE:
  normalize.py:52-54   \#+\s*REF\s*:\s*\S+   /  \*\s*REF\s*:\s*\S+   /  REF\s*:\s*\S+
  fingerprint.py:53-55 \#?\s*REF\s*:\s*\S+  /  \#?\s*REF\s+\S+  /  \*\s*REF\s*\S+

fingerprint.py additionally strips the COLON-LESS forms: '#REF 000123' and '*REF0123456'. normalize.py requires a colon in every alternative, so it does not.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
The same merchant description can therefore normalise differently here than it fingerprints. Doc 07 relies on fingerprints being stable across providers and import methods; if two paths strip different trailing markers, a card statement and a bank statement of the same purchase can produce different fingerprints and defeat Tier-3 dedup - silently, with no error, which is the exact failure mode the dedup work exists to prevent. Amex PDFs print REF markers, so this is a live path, not theoretical.

⚠️ CONSTRAINT - READ BEFORE EDITING:
fingerprint.py is hash-pinned by the 'fingerprint_frozen' invariant in invariants.yaml (sha256 bcc0ae45...). Any edit requires 'make check-invariants-update' and a deliberate commit of the new pin. The invariant exists because replay must reproduce old fingerprints exactly; changing the pattern changes every future fingerprint for affected descriptions and cannot be done silently.

DECIDE FIRST, then implement:
(a) align normalize.py to fingerprint.py's broader pattern (normalize becomes a superset), or
(b) align fingerprint.py down to normalize.py's colon-only pattern - WEAKER, it would stop stripping colon-less refs that Amex actually prints, or
(c) extract one shared pattern and have both import it, removing the duplication that let them drift.

(a) or (c) is the honest reading: fingerprint.py's broader pattern reflects real Amex output. Whichever is chosen, add a test asserting the two agree on the colon-less forms, so this cannot drift again silently.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Confirmed still open as of the 2026-10-02 Phase 2 close-out. One risk not stated in the original description, which raises the stakes on this bead:

These parsers are not incidental tooling. tools/bankparse/{amex,rabo,revolut}.py produced the measurements that docs/research/11-real-export-verification.md reports - the delta-0 reconciliation of 578 rows across 9 real statements that ADR 0003 turns into decisions, and that the new backend/finance/tests/integration/test_balance_invariant.py mirrors in its synthetic fixture. So the reference implementation is the EVIDENCE BASE for the Amex sign-flip decision, the per-account-type balance identity, and the Rabobank 24-code legend.

Consequence if left ungated: a regression in the parsers would not fail any gate, and the findings document would silently stop matching the code it describes. Nothing currently links the two, so drift would be invisible. That makes 'silently ungated' worse than the original bead assumed - it is not just untidy, it lets the evidence and the implementation disagree unnoticed.

Note the ADR 0002 decision adds a second, smaller mismatch the bead already spotted: the parsers emit provider values 'rabobank'/'revolut', which are still absent from imports.py V1_PROVIDERS, api/schemas, and frontend types.ts (all three now carry amex_pdf/rabobank_pdf/revolut_pdf per ADR 0002). title: Ratify or replace the 16 mypy explicit-any ignores (pydantic v2 incompatibility)
description:
Raised while verifying M0 (bead LifeOS-5). Currently UNRATIFIED - the orchestrator's call, needs the user's decision.

THE PROBLEM: pyproject.toml sets both mypy strict=true and disallow_any_explicit=true. That second setting is fundamentally unsatisfiable against pydantic v2. mypy's semanal check runs on the BASE CLASS EXPRESSION, and pydantic's BaseModel.__init__(self, /, **data: Any) trips it for every model - regardless of how our own fields are annotated. So every BaseModel subclass in the project produces an explicit-any error it cannot avoid.

CURRENT RESOLUTION: 16 targeted '# type: ignore[explicit-any]' comments on pydantic model class lines only. The global setting is untouched. Verified the ignores do NOT mask real Any: injecting a deliberate 'APP_ID: Any = None' in config.py is still reported by mypy. Ruff, mypy --strict and the 6 import-linter contracts all pass with this in place.

OPTIONS
  a) Keep the 16 targeted ignores. Precise, local, self-documenting at each site.
     Cost: 16 comment lines that need maintaining if models are added.
  b) Per-module disallow_any_explicit = false override for the four pydantic
     modules. Fewer comments, but a real weakening and it is invisible at the
     call site - a genuine Any in those modules would stop being caught.
  c) Drop disallow_any_explicit globally. Simplest, but loses the check
     everywhere, including the non-pydantic code where it works fine today.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), already in place. This bead exists to record that the
decision was made deliberately rather than by accident, and to revisit if the
model count grows enough for 16 ignores to become noise.

NOTE: no code change required unless you pick (b) or (c).

title: Decide psycopg wheel variant: bare 'uv sync' needs system libpq
description:
FOUND DURING P3 (bead LifeOS-pl7). Deliberately left undecided - it is a real tradeoff, not an oversight.

With neither the C extension nor a bundled libpq, every DB operation fails at first use with:

    no pq wrapper available

P3 worked around it by installing libpq5 in backend/Dockerfile, so the container is fine. But 'uv sync' on a bare developer host still hits this, which means a fresh clone is not immediately usable for DB work outside Docker.

OPTIONS
  a) psycopg[binary] - bundles its own libpq. Easiest for developers, but the
     wheels carry their own copy of the client library.
  b) keep bare psycopg and require system libpq - more explicit and matches the
     Netcup VPS target from docs/adr/0001-deployment-topology.md, but every new
     machine needs libpq-dev/libpq5 installed first.
  c) psycopg[c] - build against the system library, for distros that prefer it.

This matters for the project promise of Docker-first deployment, but the developer
experience on a bare host is currently a trap.

DECIDE deliberately and record the choice. Not blocking M0 - the container path
works. Worth settling before M1 (bead LifeOS-6) needs real migrations.

title: Add the Rabobank transaction type-code enum, sourced from the printed legend
description:
Rabobank rows carry a two-letter type code (Value date | Type | Counterparty account | Name/description | Debit amount | Credit amount). The last page of every statement prints a 24-entry legend. No enum for these codes exists anywhere in the repo.

Codes observed in the four supplied statements: ba, bg, bv, cb, db, ei, ga, id, sb, tb, we - all defined by the printed legend, no undefined codes. These matter because they carry meaning the description does not: 'ei' is a Euro direct debit and is how the American Express card payment arrives, 'tb' is an internal account transfer, 'sb' is salary.

One caveat: the 'we' entry is truncated in the source itself, reading 'we = Wero (co branded', so it cannot be resolved further. tools/bankparse/rabo.py parses the legend at runtime rather than hardcoding it.
acceptance_criteria: The type codes are enumerated in the design docs with their printed meanings, the truncation of 'we' is noted, and any consumer treats an unknown code as a parse warning rather than failing or guessing.

title: Decide how to represent the Revolut Deposit-to-IBAN mapping, which the statement does not state
description:
One Revolut statement covers two products, Account (Current Account) with 340 rows and Deposit with 11 rows, and lists two own IBANs: NL69REVO...1997 and LT5032500...9880. The statement never says which IBAN the Deposit product belongs to.

The parser currently attributes Deposit rows to the LT IBAN by inference and flags it as inferred in data/extracted/*_manifest.json. That inference is not in any doc, and an unrecorded guess baked into an import is exactly the kind of thing that becomes load-bearing by accident.

Related: import_batch has a single nullable account_id (ARCH:287) and source_record a single non-null one (ARCH:304), but this file needs two. See docs/research/11 section 3.6.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on whether the Deposit product becomes its own account, a distinct source_record status, or an explicitly inferred account_ref that surfaces for user confirmation. The inference is no longer undocumented.

title: Record the statement-balance identity as a per-account-type import invariant
description:
A current account satisfies: previous + credits - debits = closing. An Amex card satisfies: Vorig + Debiteringen - Crediteringen = Nieuw, i.e. a charge INCREASES the amount owed. Both were verified with zero delta against every supplied statement. A single generic balance self-check cannot be written for both; the identity is per account type.

No source_record or journal_line column stores a statement balance (docs/research/11 section 4 notes this under P-NO-HISTORIC-BALANCE), so the invariant is currently asserted nowhere in the design.

This invariant is what caught every parsing bug during the real-export verification: an off-by-one that mis-attached the Amex CR credit marker, a missing close-column anchor in Revolut, and a wrong sign on the Amex balance identity. It is the cheapest completeness check available and should be a required acceptance test for every new adapter.
acceptance_criteria: ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md defines the per-account-type balance identity and lists balance continuity as an acceptance criterion for every adapter. Documented as an invariant alongside the existing invariants.yaml entries.

title: M5: Enable Banking ingestion for Rabobank
description:
- RS256 JWT client (NOT HS256 - a correction to the original assumption), hand-rolled, no SDK
  - Consent flow: POST /auth -> bank redirect -> POST /sessions
  - Account linking on identification_hash, NEVER on account.uid (uid rotates at every re-auth)
  - Aggressive backfill at consent time with strategy=longest (history clamps to ~90 days shortly
    after consent, so waiting loses data permanently)
  - Polled sync - Enable Banking has NO AIS webhooks. Respect ~4 background fetches/day/ASPSP
    unless PSU headers are supplied.
  - Tier 1 dedup (entry_reference, scoped by account) + Tier 2 pending->booked
  - EXPIRED_SESSION (401) handled as a NORMAL expected re-auth flow, not an error state
  - session_ended_reason recorded as an explicit column

  entry_reference usually only materialises on BOOK, so Tier 2 cannot lean on provider IDs and must
  be confidence-scored with a review queue. Tier 3 fingerprint is computed for API rows too as a
  backstop if entry_reference ever changes on a historical re-fetch.
design: The RSA private key lives in the OS keyring, never the database. Enable Banking issues us no access or refresh tokens - the credential surface is one long-lived key.
acceptance_criteria: Rabobank consent completes end to end. A re-sync of the same window creates 0 duplicates. A PDNG->BOOK transition reconciles into ONE journal_entry, updated in place, preserving any user-set category. EXPIRED_SESSION produces a clear re-auth prompt, not a stack trace. A 90-day backfill lands in full on first consent.

title: M3: merchant normalization + 7-layer categorization
description:
Layer 1 exact user rules / 2 merchant_alias normalization / 3 known NL merchant map /
4 trigram fuzzy / 5 LEARNED FROM MANUAL CORRECTIONS / 6 LLM fallback (opt-in, deferred) /
7 uncategorized review queue.

Layer 5 is the differentiator: NEITHER reference project implements it. Firefly has no evidence of
learnability; Actual has no auto-suggest. Every manual correction raises merchant_alias.confidence to
1.0 or creates an is_learned category_rule, so the queue drains itself.

Rules must stay hand-editable: description_pattern + priority + is_learned. No generic rules DSL,
no YAML logic engine, no expression evaluator. The whole rule set should fit on one screen.
design: Reuse the merchant_alias learning mechanism for card-payment description patterns later rather than inventing a second learning store.
acceptance_criteria: Correcting 'PayPal XYZ' to Entertainment > Music means the NEXT identical transaction categorizes automatically with no hand-authored rule. The uncategorized queue is served by the idx_jl_uncat partial index. Rules are editable in the UI and readable as plain text.

assets - liabilities, snapshotted over time. Already correct from M1:
account.account_nature carries 'asset' | 'liability' | 'equity' as a first-class, indexed column,
and account_nature is what makes the Amex liability work. This milestone is aggregation only, not a

  - show the path Income -> Spending -> Savings -> Investments -> Net Worth

title: M9: budgets + recurring detection
description:
- recurring_series: detection OUTPUT, produced by a nightly job and user-confirmed
    (not user input). Deliberately not a 'recurring transaction template' like Firefly's 4-model
    Recurrence family.
  - Simple monthly budgets
  - Budget vs actual

M9 has not been started -- no code, no schema. Scope preserved in the description; reopen with 'bd undefer LifeOS-14'. Depends on M3 for recurring-merchant detection and on M1 storing real history to detect recurrence against.

title: M8: Revolut (conditional on the /aspsps probe)
description:
GATED ON LifeOS-1. Do not start before the probe result is known.

If Revolut IS in the Enable Banking production ASPSP list: add it as a second account under the
existing adapter. No new code path.

If Revolut is NOT supported: build RevolutCsvAdapter instead. Revolut's CSV export has a stable 'id'
column, so Tier 1 dedup is available there - unlike Amex.

Either way the canonical schema is unchanged. The architecture is provider-agnostic by design; only
the IdentityResolver is provider-aware.
design: This is the bead that proves the provider-agnostic claim: swapping the connectivity strategy for a whole institution changes no schema and no core logic.
acceptance_criteria: Revolut transactions import and dedup correctly via whichever path the probe selected. No change to the ledger schema.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Priority likely understated, pending verification. This bead is p3 because docs/research/07-dedup-contingencies.md:15 assumes Revolut falls back to CSV with a stable 'id' column. Two reasons that assumption is now doubtful:

(a) The user reports the Revolut app offers PDF only, so the CSV path may not exist in practice, which removes the assumed Tier-1 dedup source entirely.

(b) Research indicates Revolut may be reachable via Enable Banking PSD2 (see LifeOS-17), which would supply structured transactions with stable IDs - a better outcome than either CSV or PDF.

Do not re-prioritise on the research alone; it is unverified. Once the production probe in LifeOS-17 returns, either raise this bead to p1 (PSD2 adapter) or re-scope it explicitly to Revolut PDF history, and record which. Note that the Revolut PDF carries NO transaction IDs, so the PDF path is Tier-3 fingerprint only, and the 34 To Savings vs 9 From Savings imbalance in docs/research/11 section 3.6 remains unresolvable by matching.
